newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rates reflect fundamentals - MOF minister.
newsitem.headline: Japan rates reflect fundamentals - MOF minister.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday that he believes Japan's long-term market interest rates are currently reflecting economic fundamentals.

Mitsuzuka, responding to questions about news earlier in the day that government officials said they found long-term interest rates to be low in view of the economy, said: "In the current state, I believe it (interest rates) is reflecting fundamentals."
Senior government officials told Reuters earlier that recent rises in yen bond prices were not in line with the performance of the economy, in which production has begun to show some strength.
Meanwhile, Mitsuzuka reiterated that his ministry will work towards setting up an independent watchdog for financial institutions as part of Japan's financial reforms.
"As I keep repeating, our basic policy to work in line with the agreement reached by the coalition parties has not changed," Mitsuzuka told reporters.

Media reports on Wednesday said MOF officials circulated a report to politicians in the Liberal Democratic Party opposing a plan to set up an independent watchdog modelled after the Fair Trade Commission (FTC).

Mitsuzuka said the report by MOF officials to politicians was only to explain the ministry's opinion and was not intended to influence politicians and disrupt the agreement the LDP reached with the Socialist and Sakigake parties, with which the minority LDP government has a loose alliance.
